36:# Tuition and Fees
42:## Understanding the Tuition Rates Workbook
44:The tuition rates workbook includes current tuition and segregated fee rates charged to students.  The full schedule is found under the ‘Tuition and Fee Schedule’ tab. Students are also able to search for specific tuition rates by major and degree level under the ‘Tuition Rates by Program and Degree Level’ tab. Tuition rates include [segregated fees](https://bursar.wisc.edu/tuition-and-fees/segregated-fees).
48:[View Tuition Rates Workbook](https://viz.wisc.edu/views/TuitionandSegregatedFeeRatesforAcademicPrograms/HomePage?%3Aembed=y&%3Aiid=1&%3AisGuestRedirectFromVizportal=y)
54:Fall and Spring term rates are set in late July or early August, and the workbook is updated as soon as possible after that. Rates for Summer term are usually posted in late March.
56:## Fall 2026 Tuition Announcement
58:The UW System Board of Regents approved a plan for tuition increases for Universities of Wisconsin undergraduate students for the 2026/2027 academic year.
60:[Learn More about the Fall 2026 increase](https://bursar.wisc.edu/tuition-and-fees/fall-2026-increase)
90:## Other Types of Fees
92:In addition to tuition, there are other fees that may be assessed on a student’s account.  Some of these fees are one-time fees; others may be assessed each semester depending on the student’s status, enrollment date, courses taken and if the student is living in University Housing.
94:- [Segregated Fees](https://bursar.wisc.edu/tuition-and-fees/segregated-fees) are charges, in addition to tuition, assessed to all students. Segregated fees pay for student services, activities, programs, and facilities that support the mission of University of Wisconsin System institutions, including UW–Madison.
96:- [eTextbook Fee](https://bursar.wisc.edu/etextbook-fee) is charged to students who register for courses participating in the e-text program
97:- [Registrar Office Document Fee](https://registrar.wisc.edu/fines-fees-and-holds/#docfee) is a mandatory one-time fee that covers the cost of official university documents (such as transcripts).
98:- [New Student Fee](https://newstudent.wisc.edu/about-us/funding/) is charged to all undergraduates in their first semester.
99:- [FSL Community Contribution Fee](https://fsl.wisc.edu/fsl-community-contribution-fee/) is charged to each fraternity and sorority member every semester.
100:- [International Services Fee](https://iss.wisc.edu/international-student-fee-increase/) is applicable to students who are at UW–Madison on F1 or J1 visas and supports the International Student Services office.
101:- [Late Registration Fee](https://registrar.wisc.edu/fines-fees-and-holds/) is assessed to students who begin enrolling in courses after a specific date each term.
105:[Tuition adjustment and refund](https://bursar.wisc.edu/tuition-and-fees/tuition-adjustment) is dependent on a number of factors, including the student’s academic program, number of credits taken and the date the drop occurs.  Students should review the [tuition adjustment calendar](https://registrar.wisc.edu/dates/) and work with their academic advisor before dropping a class.

Interact with a scraped page in a live browser session. Run AI prompts or
execute code against any previous scrape.

Arguments:

Options:

  -p, --prompt <text>         AI prompt (alternative to positional argument)
  -s, --scrape-id <id>        Scrape job ID (default: last scrape)
  --node                      Execute code as Node.js/Playwright (default)
                              (default: false)

  --json                      Output as JSON format (default: false)

content.text:
All three schools have posted 2026-27 rates on their own sites, so none of the figures below fall back to 2025-26. I pulled each one fresh from the official pages on 2026-10-17.

## 1. Ohio State, Columbus (Tuition Guarantee cohort "TG27", first-years starting Autumn 2026)
Source: https://registrar.osu.edu/student-hub/tuition-and-fees/undergraduate-tuition-and-fees-2026-2027/undergraduate-fees-students-that-began-summer-2026-or-after-2026-2027/
The page says these are "for first-year students beginning Autumn 2026, Spring 2027, and Summer 2027." The table below is "COLUMBUS CAMPUS FEES – On Campus | Autumn and Spring", using the 12–18 credit flat rate. Annual figures are the per-semester amount times 2, which I calculated.

| Item | Per semester | Per year |
|---|---|---|
| Instructional Fee (Ohio State's word for tuition) | $6,460.50 | $12,921.00 |
| General Fee | $297.00 | $594.00 |
| Student Activity Fee | $42.00 | $84.00 |
| Recreational Fee | $137.50 | $275.00 |
| Student Union Facility Fee | $74.40 | $148.80 |
| COTA Bus Service Fee | $13.50 | $27.00 |
| **Total** | **$7,024.90** | **$14,049.80** |

1. **Tuition:** $12,921.00 a year (Instructional Fee only).
2. **Mandatory fees:** $1,128.80 a year (General plus the four flat fees). If the General Fee is counted with tuition, as the admissions page does, the split is $13,515 tuition and $534.80 fees.
3. **Total:** $14,049.80, which the school rounds to **$14,050**.
4. **Does the headline include fees?** Yes. $14,050 appears on https://undergrad.osu.edu/cost-and-aid/basic-costs ("Estimated, 2026-2027 academic year … Ohio resident Columbus: $14,050"). That page labels it "Tuition (includes instructional and general fees)", but the number actually equals all six fees. The registrar says the guarantee covers "instructional, general, student activity, student union, recreational and COTA fees." Ohio State's news release says the same: "$14,050 for Ohio residents starting in autumn 2026."
5. **URLs:** given above.
6. **2026-27 confirmed?** Yes.
- **Differential charges:** Some programs add Learning Technology and Program fees. For example, Engineering is $240 plus $2,000 per semester and Business is $186 plus $649.20 per semester. Arts and Sciences has none.
- **Discrepancy:** The financial aid cost-of-attendance page (https://sfa.osu.edu/incoming-freshmen/about-aid/financial-aid-eligibility) lists "Tuition and fees $14,034" for 2026-27, $16 less than the registrar total. I could not find the reason.

## 2. University of Oregon (2026-27 Tuition Cohort "GTUIT2627", Eugene campus, not Honors College)
Sources:
- Board-approved fee tables PDF ("Approved by the Board of Trustees on March 17, 2026"): https://pages.uoregon.edu/baoforms/files/brp/Fees/2026-2027%20Tuition%20and%20Fee%20Tables.pdf
- Cohort page: https://vpfa.uoregon.edu/tuition/undergraduate-2026-tuition-cohort-tuition-and-fees (its own tables load in Power BI, which didn't render in my scrape, so the numbers come from the PDF).

**Credit assumption:** The financial aid page says costs are "based on typical enrollment for new incoming undergraduates of 15 credits for each of three terms, totaling 45 credits per year."

1. **Tuition:** $322.93 per credit. 15 credits is $4,843.95 per term, or **$14,531.85** a year. There is no flat-rate plateau; tuition rises with every credit.
2. **Mandatory fees, per term:** Building $45.00, Health Service $280.00, Recreation Center $177.50, Student Union $247.00, Technology $70.25, ASUO Incidental $161.25. The PDF's "Total Mandatory Fees" is $981.00 per term, so **$2,943.00** a year.
   - A one-time Matriculation Fee of $569.89 is charged to all new students in their first term. The financial aid page rounds it to $570 and leaves it out of its headline.
3. **Total:** $17,474.85, rounded to **$17,475**. The financial aid page (https://financialaid.uoregon.edu/cost_of_attendance) says "2026–27 Estimated … Resident Costs: Tuition and Fees* $17,475". Add the matriculation fee and a first year costs about $18,045.
4. **Does the headline include fees?** Yes: "The undergraduate cost of attendance includes mandatory fees all students must pay." The footnote says it "Does not include the one-time matriculation fee of $570."
5. **URLs:** given above.
6. **2026-27 confirmed?** Yes.
- **Differential tuition:** Business School courses cost an extra $50 per credit for this cohort. Clark Honors College adds $1,022.73 per term.
- **Data issue:** On the cohort page, the link labelled "2026-27 Tuition and Mandatory Fees document" actually points to the 2025-26 PDF.

## 3. Penn State, University Park (Pennsylvania resident, lower division, freshman/sophomore)
Sources:
- Tuition: https://tuition.psu.edu/rates-effective-2026-fall-semester ("University Park – Rates Effective 2026 Fall Semester")
- Fee: https://tuition.psu.edu/2026-27-student-initiated-fee-semester ("2026-27 Student Initiated Fee Per Semester, Fall and Spring 2026-27")

1. **Tuition:** "Freshmen & Sophomore | Per Academic Year 20,878 | Full-Time Per Semester 10,439 | Part-Time Per Credit 870." That is **$20,878** a year, a flat rate for 12–19 credits. The page notes "Academic year is Fall and Spring semesters."
2. **Mandatory fees:** The Student Initiated Fee is the only one: "University Park | 9 or More Credits 320.00" per semester, so **$640** a year. The bursar page (https://www.bursar.psu.edu/fees) says "The Student Fee is mandatory." Penn State lists no other mandatory fee for domestic students. New international undergraduates pay an extra $750 per semester.
3. **Total:** **$21,518**, which I added up myself.
4. **Does the headline include fees?** No. The admissions page (https://www.psu.edu/admission/undergraduate/tuition-costs, "2026-2027 Penn State Costs: University Park") lists Tuition $20,878 and Student Initiated Fee $640 on separate lines. I found no single tuition-plus-fees figure on a Penn State page.
5. **URLs:** given above.
6. **2026-27 confirmed?** Yes. The tuition site says the Board approved 2026-27 tuition and mandatory fees on July 18, 2025.
- **Differential tuition:** Freshmen in all majors pay the same rate. It splits at upper division (juniors and seniors): Science/IST/EMS $24,794; Business, Engineering and Nursing $26,778; all other programs $22,520.

## Summary (resident, 2026-27, per academic year)
| School | Tuition | Mandatory fees | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ohio State Columbus (TG27) | $12,921.00 | $1,128.80 | $14,049.80 (published as $14,050) |
| Oregon (2026 cohort, 45 credits) | $14,531.85 | $2,943.00, plus $569.89 one-time | $17,474.85 (published as $17,475) |
| Penn State UP (lower division) | $20,878 | $640 | $21,518 |

The scraped pages are saved in /tmp/fceval-a3-t1-uzi931ho/work/.firecrawl/: osu-2026.md, uo-pdf.md, uo-coa.md, psu.md, psu-sif.md and psu-fees.md.

1. **Tuition:** $322.93 per credit. 15 credits is $4,843.95 per term, or **$14,531.85** a year. There is no flat-rate plateau; tuition rises with every credit.
2. **Mandatory fees, per term:** Building $45.00, Health Service $280.00, Recreation Center $177.50, Student Union $247.00, Technology $70.25, ASUO Incidental $161.25. The PDF's "Total Mandatory Fees" is $981.00 per term, so **$2,943.00** a year.
   - A one-time Matriculation Fee of $569.89 is charged to all new students in their first term. The financial aid page rounds it to $570 and leaves it out of its headline.
3. **Total:** $17,474.85, rounded to **$17,475**. The financial aid page (https://financialaid.uoregon.edu/cost_of_attendance) says "2026–27 Estimated … Resident Costs: Tuition and Fees* $17,475". Add the matriculation fee and a first year costs about $18,045.
4. **Does the headline include fees?** Yes: "The undergraduate cost of attendance includes mandatory fees all students must pay." The footnote says it "Does not include the one-time matriculation fee of $570."
5. **URLs:** given above.
6. **2026-27 confirmed?** Yes.
- **Differential tuition:** Business School courses cost an extra $50 per credit for this cohort. Clark Honors College adds $1,022.73 per term.
- **Data issue:** On the cohort page, the link labelled "2026-27 Tuition and Mandatory Fees document" actually points to the 2025-26 PDF.

## 3. Penn State, University Park (Pennsylvania resident, lower division, freshman/sophomore)
Sources:
- Tuition: https://tuition.psu.edu/rates-effective-2026-fall-semester ("University Park – Rates Effective 2026 Fall Semester")
- Fee: https://tuition.psu.edu/2026-27-student-initiated-fee-semester ("2026-27 Student Initiated Fee Per Semester, Fall and Spring 2026-27")

1. **Tuition:** "Freshmen & Sophomore | Per Academic Year 20,878 | Full-Time Per Semester 10,439 | Part-Time Per Credit 870." That is **$20,878** a year, a flat rate for 12–19 credits. The page notes "Academic year is Fall and Spring semesters."
2. **Mandatory fees:** The Student Initiated Fee is the only one: "University Park | 9 or More Credits 320.00" per semester, so **$640** a year. The bursar page (https://www.bursar.psu.edu/fees) says "The Student Fee is mandatory." Penn State lists no other mandatory fee for domestic students. New international undergraduates pay an extra $750 per semester.
3. **Total:** **$21,518**, which I added up myself.
4. **Does the headline include fees?** No. The admissions page (https://www.psu.edu/admission/undergraduate/tuition-costs, "2026-2027 Penn State Costs: University Park") lists Tuition $20,878 and Student Initiated Fee $640 on separate lines. I found no single tuition-plus-fees figure on a Penn State page.
5. **URLs:** given above.
6. **2026-27 confirmed?** Yes. The tuition site says the Board approved 2026-27 tuition and mandatory fees on July 18, 2025.
- **Differential tuition:** Freshmen in all majors pay the same rate. It splits at upper division (juniors and seniors): Science/IST/EMS $24,794; Business, Engineering and Nursing $26,778; all other programs $22,520.

# IU holds in-state undergraduate tuition flat for 2025-27
_**EDITOR’S NOTE:** This story was updated on June 12, 2025, to reflect the IU Board of Trustees’ approval._
BLOOMINGTON, Ind. — The Indiana University Board of Trustees approved holding tuition and mandatory fees for in-state undergraduate students flat for the next two years, reflecting the university’s commitment to access and affordability.
The IU Board of Trustees held a public forum on tuition and fees for the 2025-27 academic years at 12:15 p.m. Thursday, June 12, at IU Bloomington’s Henke Hall of Champions.
![An IU trident adorns a limestone gate outside the Indiana Memorial Union](https://news.iu.edu/live/image/gid/2/width/500/height/333/4050_6308f1560c8d2_yoiijzs3jn_actual.jpg)[Image - 1:View print quality image about An IU trident adorns a limestone gate outside the Indiana Memorial Union](https://news.iu.edu/live/image/gid/2/width/500/height/333/4050_6308f1560c8d2_yoiijzs3jn_actual.jpg "Image - 1:View print quality image about An IU trident adorns a limestone gate outside the Indiana Memorial Union")IU remains committed to making higher education more affordable for Hoosiers with its recommendation to hold in-state undergraduate tuition flat for the next two years.
While IU leaders proposed no increase in tuition or mandatory fees for in-state undergraduate students, the board approved a tuition increase of up to 2% for graduate programs, with an exception for some programs in the health and medical fields. The increase will support market demand and allow IU to offer high-quality programs at a sustainable cost.
With student success at the heart of its IU 2030 strategic plan, IU remains committed to making higher education more affordable for Hoosiers. Beginning in fiscal year 2024, the university [reduced the number of academic fees by half](https://today.iu.edu/live/news/3414-restructure-of-fees-adds-clarity-generally-reduces), saving the student body as a whole $14.5 million a year. Fundraising in 2024 included a 23 percent increase in support for student access and affordability.
[Details of the recommended tuition and fees](https://finance.iu.edu/doc/2025-2027-tuition-and-fee-schedule-recommended.pdf) are available on the website of the [Office of the Executive Vice President for Finance and Administration](https://finance.iu.edu/).

content.text:
I found official 2026-27 figures for all three schools. Each one is published on the school's own site, so none of these numbers falls back to 2025-26.

## 1. University of Southern California (private, so there is no in-state rate)
- **Tuition: $75,384 a year.** The page says "Tuition (12-18 units for two semesters) | $75,384". The registrar charges $37,692 per semester for Fall 2026 (it lists "Undergraduate Students (12-18 units) … Fall 2026 $37,692").
- **Mandatory fees: $1,952 a year** ("Fees | $1,952"). The Financial Aid page does not break this down. The itemized Fall 2026 rates I found, each multiplied by two semesters:
  - Student Health Center fee: $720 + $720 = $1,440 (Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 at $720 each, from studenthealth.usc.edu)
  - Student Programming Fee (undergraduate): $64 × 2 = $128
  - Transportation Fee: $151 × 2 = $302
  - Norman H. Topping Student Aid Fund: $11 × 2 = $22
  - These add up to $1,892, which is **$60 short of $1,952**. I could not find what covers the gap. The graduate cost page lists a "Disability Insurance $40" line, but the undergraduate pages don't show anything similar.
  - One-time charges on top of that: "Add $450 new student fee for your first semester." Health insurance is billed separately unless waived.
- **Total: $77,336**, or **$77,786** for a first-year student once the $450 new student fee is added.
- **Headline:** the cost-of-attendance table shows tuition and fees as separate lines. The page says "Tuition is the same for both in-state and out-of-state residents."
- **Sources:** https://financialaid.usc.edu/undergraduate-financial-aid/cost-of-attendance/ (shows both 2026-27 and 2025-26 tables; 2025-26 was $73,260 + $1,902), https://arr.usc.edu/tuition-and-fees/ and https://studenthealth.usc.edu/fees-deadlines
- **2026-27 confirmed:** yes.

## 2. University of Washington Seattle (Washington resident, 3 quarters)
- **Tuition: $12,664.** This is the Operating Fee of $11,928 plus the Building Fee of $736.
- **Mandatory fees: $1,209.** Tech Fee $114, Services & Activities Fee $546, IMA Bond $96, Facilities Renovation $210 and U-PASS $243.
  - First-year students also pay the one-time New Student Enrollment & Orientation Fee: $467.
- **Total:** the official "Total Incl U-PASS" is **$13,873**, or **$14,340** for a first-year student including the orientation fee. Before U-PASS, "Total Tuition and Fees" is $13,630.
- **Headline:** Financial Aid's "Tuition & Fees: $13,873" includes the mandatory fees, so the official headline figure covers them.
- **Sources:**
  - https://finance.uw.edu/tuition-fees/files/docs/annual-tuition-and-fees/2026-2027tricampusannualtuitionandfees.pdf (itemized row: "Undergraduate | $11,928 | $736 | $12,664 | $114 | $546 | $96 | $210 | $13,630 | $243 | $13,873")
  - https://www.washington.edu/opb/tuition-fees/estimated-annual-cost-of-attendance-for-first-year-undergraduates/ (now redirects to finance.uw.edu; it gives the orientation fee and says resident tuition rose 3.3%, "approved by the UW Board of Regents in June 2026")
  - https://www.washington.edu/financialaid/cost-of-attendance/
- **2026-27 confirmed:** yes.
- **Conflict:** the Admissions page (https://admit.washington.edu/costs/coa/) is labeled 2026-27 but shows "Resident tuition $13,406" and non-resident $44,460. A note on the same page says it includes a "$210" U-Pass. Neither figure matches the finance office or Financial Aid, so it looks stale. I would trust the finance office PDF.

## 3. University of Wisconsin–Madison (Wisconsin resident, base rate)
- **Tuition: $10,716.61** ("New Full-Time Resident Tuition Rate"). That is a 2% increase from $10,506.48.
- **Segregated fees: $1,699.48 a year**, which is $849.74 per semester. The per-semester breakdown (undergraduate, Fall 2026 or Spring 2027):
  - University Health Services: $318.00
  - Wisconsin Union: $179.64
  - Recreation & Wellbeing (General): $109.20
  - Union Building Projects: $76.68
  - Recreation & Wellbeing (Master Plan): $69.24
  - Bus pass and transportation services: $48.75
  - General student service fund: $15.34
  - Associated Students of Madison: $14.19
  - Child Care Tuition Assistance Program: $12.00
  - Campus radio fund: $5.50
  - Municipal services: $1.20
- **Total: $12,416.09.** The page says "New Total Tuition & Segregated Fee Rate for the 26-27 Academic Year | $12,416.09".
  - One-time charges for first-year students: the Registrar Document Fee ("This $130 one-time fee") and a New Student Fee, which Financial Aid estimates at $330.
- **Headline:** the Bursar says "Tuition rates include segregated fees", so the headline figure includes them.

# Regents approve 2026–27 tuition increase for UI students
The Iowa Board of Regents has approved a tuition increase for University of Iowa students to address effects of inflation and maintain the excellent quality of public higher education, research, and services.
At its April 23 meeting, the board approved a $287 increase to base tuition for undergraduate resident students and a $475 increase for undergraduate nonresident students. For graduate students, the approved tuition increase is $360 for resident students and $464 for nonresident students. The increases will take effect at the start of the fall 2026 semester.
Undergraduate resident tuition and fees at Iowa remain among the most affordable for students in the university’s peer group.
![Chart showing 2025-26 undergraduate tuition and fees comparison of universities](https://now.uiowa.edu/sites/now.uiowa.edu/files/2026-04/IOWANOW-TuitionComparison-Chart-2026-1.png)
- The Tippie College of Business will eliminate the system of different tuition rates for Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) students based on completed college credits and have a base $13,052 tuition rate for resident students and a $35,328 tuition rate for nonresident students.
- To pay for additional services required for economics majors now that the undergraduate program has moved from the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences to the Tippie College of Business, new students in the major will have a tuition rate of $11,852 for resident students and $34,128 for nonresidents.
Some graduate and professional colleges will keep their tuition rates flat, while the board approved slightly higher increases for specific programs based on costs.
Tuition increases were approved for the following:
The board also approved a mandatory student fee increase of $62 for undergraduate students and $55 for graduate students. The extra funds will go toward technology, health and mental health services, student activities, modernizing student spaces, and recreation.

All three schools have 2026-27 resident undergraduate figures posted on their own sites. Nothing below is a 2025-26 fallback.

## Summary (resident, full-time, fall + spring)

| School | Tuition | Mandatory fees | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| UIUC (base rate, new students) | $13,252 | $5,182 ($3,430 without the waivable health insurance) | $18,434 ($16,682 without insurance) |
| IU Bloomington | $10,621.84 | $1,522.04 | $12,143.88 (COA page shows $12,142) |
| Univ. of Iowa (Liberal Arts & Sciences) | $9,852 | $2,119 | $11,971 |

---

## 1. University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign: 2026-27 confirmed

- **Tuition: $13,252/yr.** The page "2026 - 2027 Undergrad Base Tuition Rates" lists the row "Summer 2026 through Spring 2027 (guaranteed rate)" with Resident Rate $13,252.00.
  - Source: https://cost.illinois.edu/Home/UgradBase?DiffCode=BASE&TermCode=120268&TableType=1 (linked from https://registrar.illinois.edu/ug-tuition-rates-2627/)
  - The base rate covers LAS majors (with exceptions), Applied Health Sciences, Education, Exploratory Studies, Social Work and a few ACES majors.
- **Mandatory campus fees: $2,591 per semester, $5,182/yr.** The page is "26/27 1U Fees by Credit Range, Fall 2026 & Spring 2027", Range I (12+ hours). Items per semester:
  - Service $356, General $309, Health Insurance $876, Health Service $259, Transportation $74, Student Initiated $82, AFMFA $379, Library & IT $256.
  - Source: https://registrar.illinois.edu/tuition-fees/tuition-fee-rates/tf-rates-term/ug-fees-cr-2627/
  - The page says fees "except health insurance, are mandatory." Health insurance ($876 per semester, $1,752/yr) is the only fee that can be waived. Without it, fees are $1,715 per semester, or $3,430/yr.
  - The registrar's 2026-27 expenses page confirms "Campus Fees $5,182", with a footnote: "Includes $1,752 for student health insurance which can be waived." Source: https://registrar.illinois.edu/tuition-fees/tuition-fee-rates/tf-rates-academic-year/ug-additional-expenses-2627/
- **Headline number includes fees.** The admissions page says "Estimates are based on 2026-2027 data" and gives resident "Tuition & Fees $18,530–$24,018" (https://www.admissions.illinois.edu/tuition/).
  - $18,530 is $96 more than my $18,434. The nonresident figure is off by the same $96. I could not find what the $96 is on any official page, so it is unresolved. It may be a one-time new-student charge.
- **Notes:**
  - Illinois Truth in Tuition guarantees the rate for 4 years, so the rate depends on entry cohort. Students who entered in 2025-26 pay $12,992.
  - Program-based tiers cost more than the base rate. They are ACE, ACES 1, ACES 2, Astrophysics, Business, Chemistry & Life Sciences, Economics, Engineering (which includes CS+X), Fine & Applied Arts, Information Sciences, Kinesiology and Media. Each is linked from the ug-tuition-rates-2627 page. I did not scrape each tier's amount. The top of the admissions range ($24,018) suggests the highest tier.
  - MCB 250/251/252/253/450 each carry $320 of course-based tuition.

## 2. Indiana University Bloomington: 2026-27 confirmed

- **Tuition: $10,621.84/yr. Combined mandatory fee: $1,522.04/yr. Total: $12,143.88.** These come from IU's 2025-27 operating budget schedule, Bloomington resident, 2026-27 column. The same figures appear for 2024-25 and 2025-26, so resident tuition is flat.
  - Source: https://finance.iu.edu/doc/2025-2027-tuition-and-fee-schedule-recommended.pdf
  - The PDF is titled "RECOMMENDED". IU News says the Board of Trustees approved holding "tuition and mandatory fees for in-state undergraduate students flat for the next two years" on June 12, 2025 (https://news.iu.edu/live/news/45837-iu-holds-in-state-undergraduate-tuition-flat-for-2025-).
- **Fee itemization.** IU now charges one mandatory fee: "Student Services Fee >6 Hours: $761.02 per term, Mandatory, Bloomington". That works out to $1,522.04/yr. Source: https://academics.iu.edu/fees/index.html?fee_term=Fall%202026&fee_type=Mandatory%20Fee
- **Headline number includes fees.** The cost-of-attendance page labels it "Cost of attendance for full-time, domestic undergraduate students in 2026–2027" and shows "Tuition and mandatory fees | $12,142 | $42,702" (https://bloomington.iu.edu/cost-aid/cost-attendance/undergraduate.html).
  - This is about $2 below the schedule's $12,143.88, probably rounding.
- **Notes:**
  - The tuition is a flat rate covering "40 credit hours across fall, spring, and our intersessions." Summer is charged per credit hour.
  - Program differentials are added on top. In the schedule, Business is $1,549.86 and Pre-Business $774.94. Other differentials (Science, Informatics, Music, Nursing, O'Neill, Public Health, Social Work, Education, Media) range from about $118 to $4,694.
  - An older studentcentral.indiana.edu image still shows "$11,220". It looks stale, so I ignored it.
  - I could not get the Fall 2026 undergraduate tuition row out of the paginated University Fee List.

## 3. University of Iowa: 2026-27 confirmed

- **Tuition: $4,926.00 per semester, $9,852/yr.** **Mandatory fees: $1,059.50 per semester, $2,119/yr.** **Total: $5,985.50 per semester, $11,971/yr.** All from the registrar's tuition tables, headed "Tuition & Fees Fall 2026", Liberal Arts & Sciences (1001), Undergraduate Resident, 12+ hours.
  - Source: https://tuition.ais.its.uiowa.edu/
  - Fees per semester: Technology $320.50, Activities $42, Services $46, Student Union $66.50, Building $78, Recreation Facility $180, Arts & Cultural Events $17, Career Services $16.50, Student Health $147, Mental Health $26, IMU Facilities $120.
  - The page I scraped showed Fall 2026. I got the annual figure by doubling it, which matches the financial aid page's $11,971.
- **Headline number includes fees.** The financial aid page shows "Undergraduate - Living On or Off Campus, 2026-2027: Tuition & fees* $11,971" (https://financialaid.uiowa.edu/cost). Admissions shows the same figure: https://admissions.uiowa.edu/finances/estimated-costs-attendance
  - Its footnote reads: "The tuition listed is estimated and is based on the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences. Tuition rates are finalized each summer... by the State of Iowa Board of Regents."
  - The Regents approved the rates on April 23, 2026: base resident tuition is "2026-27 $9,852" (up $287 from $9,565), and mandatory fees rose $62 (https://now.uiowa.edu/news/2026/04/regents-approve-2026-27-tuition-increase-ui-students).
- **Notes:**
  - First-year students are also billed a one-time $250 University Records and Documents Fee in their first semester. It is not part of the $11,971.
  - Program rates are higher. Per the admissions page, totals with fees are: Business $15,382, Engineering first-year $13,581 (later years $15,702), Nursing $15,701, and Radiation Sciences / Nuclear Medicine Technology $14,675. CS 3rd and 4th year tuition is $5,515.50 per semester.

Scraped pages are saved in /tmp/fceval-a3-t1-uzi931ho/work/.firecrawl/ (uiuc_*.md, iu_*.md, iowa_*.md).

- **Headline number includes fees.** The cost-of-attendance page labels it "Cost of attendance for full-time, domestic undergraduate students in 2026–2027" and shows "Tuition and mandatory fees | $12,142 | $42,702" (https://bloomington.iu.edu/cost-aid/cost-attendance/undergraduate.html).
  - This is about $2 below the schedule's $12,143.88, probably rounding.
- **Notes:**
  - The tuition is a flat rate covering "40 credit hours across fall, spring, and our intersessions." Summer is charged per credit hour.
  - Program differentials are added on top. In the schedule, Business is $1,549.86 and Pre-Business $774.94. Other differentials (Science, Informatics, Music, Nursing, O'Neill, Public Health, Social Work, Education, Media) range from about $118 to $4,694.
  - An older studentcentral.indiana.edu image still shows "$11,220". It looks stale, so I ignored it.
  - I could not get the Fall 2026 undergraduate tuition row out of the paginated University Fee List.

## 3. University of Iowa: 2026-27 confirmed

- **Tuition: $4,926.00 per semester, $9,852/yr.** **Mandatory fees: $1,059.50 per semester, $2,119/yr.** **Total: $5,985.50 per semester, $11,971/yr.** All from the registrar's tuition tables, headed "Tuition & Fees Fall 2026", Liberal Arts & Sciences (1001), Undergraduate Resident, 12+ hours.
  - Source: https://tuition.ais.its.uiowa.edu/
  - Fees per semester: Technology $320.50, Activities $42, Services $46, Student Union $66.50, Building $78, Recreation Facility $180, Arts & Cultural Events $17, Career Services $16.50, Student Health $147, Mental Health $26, IMU Facilities $120.
  - The page I scraped showed Fall 2026. I got the annual figure by doubling it, which matches the financial aid page's $11,971.
- **Headline number includes fees.** The financial aid page shows "Undergraduate - Living On or Off Campus, 2026-2027: Tuition & fees* $11,971" (https://financialaid.uiowa.edu/cost). Admissions shows the same figure: https://admissions.uiowa.edu/finances/estimated-costs-attendance
  - Its footnote reads: "The tuition listed is estimated and is based on the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences. Tuition rates are finalized each summer... by the State of Iowa Board of Regents."
  - The Regents approved the rates on April 23, 2026: base resident tuition is "2026-27 $9,852" (up $287 from $9,565), and mandatory fees rose $62 (https://now.uiowa.edu/news/2026/04/regents-approve-2026-27-tuition-increase-ui-students).
- **Notes:**
  - First-year students are also billed a one-time $250 University Records and Documents Fee in their first semester. It is not part of the $11,971.
  - Program rates are higher. Per the admissions page, totals with fees are: Business $15,382, Engineering first-year $13,581 (later years $15,702), Nursing $15,701, and Radiation Sciences / Nuclear Medicine Technology $14,675. CS 3rd and 4th year tuition is $5,515.50 per semester.

I found official 2026-27 figures for all three schools, and each is posted for 2026-27 (not just 2025-26). All amounts are per academic year for a full-time in-state first-year.

## Summary

| School | Tuition | Mandatory fees | Total | Headline includes fees? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Purdue West Lafayette (base, Indiana resident) | $9,718 | $274 | **$9,992** | Yes |
| Rutgers–New Brunswick (School of Arts and Sciences, NJ resident) | $15,381 | $4,008 | **$19,389** | No, listed separately |
| UCLA (CA resident, fall 2026 cohort) | $14,202 | $2,558.71 (registrar) | **$16,760.71** (registrar) / **$16,430** (financial aid) | See notes |

## 1. Purdue University West Lafayette
- **Source:** https://www.purdue.edu/treasurer/finance/bursar-office/tuition/fee-rates-2026-2027/undergraduate-tuition-and-fees-2026-2027/ (page title "Undergraduate Tuition and Fees – 2026-2027", confirmed for 2026-27).
- **Tuition:** Purdue calls it "General Service": $4,859 per semester, $9,718 per year.
- **Fees:**
  - Student Fitness and Wellness Fee: $234
  - Student Activity Fee: $40
- **Total:** "Sub-Total Tuition: $4,996.00 / $9,992.00". The headline number includes the mandatory fees.
- **Tuition freeze:** the trustees' release says "Tuition and mandatory fees will remain frozen for all undergraduate students at Purdue's main campus (Indianapolis and West Lafayette) for the 13th and 14th consecutive years, in particular keeping base undergraduate tuition and fees for Indiana residents under $10,000 per year." The 2025-26 bursar page shows the same $9,992. Source: https://www.purdue.edu/newsroom/2025/Q2/trustees-approve-2026-budget-frozen-base-tuition-for-main-campus-and-no-increase-for-indiana-residents-at-purdue-northwest-and-purdue-fort-wayne-for-2025-26-2026-27/

| Program | Differential | Total |

  - Official rate sheet: "2026-2027 New Brunswick Undergraduate.xlsx", linked from https://finance.rutgers.edu/student-abc/tuition-fees ("approved... for the 2026-2027 academic year on July 9, 2026"). Direct link: https://rutgers.box.com/v/nb-ug-tuition-fees
- **Figures** (all three sources agree): Tuition $15,381, Fees $4,008, "Sub-total of Direct Charges $19,389". The headline shows tuition and fees as separate lines.
- **Fee breakdown** (rate sheet, per semester × 2; the sheet marks these "*Mandatory Fees"):
  - Student Fee: $1,594 per semester, $3,188 per year
  - School Fee (SAS): $189 per semester, $378 per year
  - Technology Fee: $221 per semester, $442 per year
  - These sum to $4,008. Tuition is $7,690.50 per semester.

| School | Tuition | Fees |
|---|---|---|

| Mason Gross | $15,945 | $4,866 |
| School of Environmental and Biological Sciences | $17,286 (per year, from rate sheet) | n/a |

- **Primary source:** Registrar "Annual and Term Student Fees", https://sa.ucla.edu/RO/Fees/Public/public-fees. This is a dynamic page; the figures appear after selecting 2026-2027 / Annual / "Undergraduate cohort 2026-27". Confirmed for 2026-27.
- **Resident amounts, per year:**
  - UC Tuition: $14,202.00
  - Student Services Fee: $1,386.00
  - Campus and other fees, totalling $1,172.71:
    - UCSA $7.00
    - Ackerman Student Union $81.00
    - Arts Restoring Community $6.66
    - Bruin Bash $5.78
    - Good Clothes Good People Basic Needs $1.24
    - Green Initiative $14.40
    - Instructional Enhancement Initiative $324.00
    - PLEDGE $72.58
    - SPARC $150.00
    - Student Seismic $113.00
    - Undergraduate Students Association $331.65
    - Wooden Center $45.00
    - Universal Access Transit Pass $20.40
  - UC Student Health Insurance Plan: $3,886.02 (waivable)
  - Document Fee: $200.96 (one-time, new students)
- **Totals:**
  - Without health insurance or the Document Fee: **$16,760.71**
  - The page's own totals include health insurance: "Continuing student total mandatory fees $20,646.73"; "New student total mandatory fees $20,847.69"
- **Financial aid page:** https://financialaid.ucla.edu/go/coa, under "New Students Starting in the 2026-27 Academic Year": "University Fees (UC Systemwide Tuition: $15,588, Campus fees: $842) $16,430". There, $15,588 is UC Tuition plus the Student Services Fee, and health insurance is a separate line ($3,885, "can be waived").
- **Discrepancy:** the financial aid page lists campus fees of $842, while the registrar's itemized campus fees add up to $1,172.71 ($330.71 more). Both pages say the figures "may not be final". The registrar is the billing source.

- **Differential tuition:** none for Letters & Science undergraduates.

content.text:
I found published 2026-27 figures on the schools' own sites for all 18. No school needed a 2025-26 fallback. Six research agents read the pages on 2026-10-17; I didn't re-open them myself, but the agents quote each page and the copies are saved in `.firecrawl/`.

**How I compared them.** Each total is resident tuition plus recurring mandatory fees for two semesters (three quarters at Northwestern and Washington, three terms at Oregon). It uses the general or Arts & Sciences rate and the rate for students entering in fall 2026. Health insurance that students can waive and one-time new-student fees are left out. Where the bursar's line items and the financial aid "Tuition & fees" figure disagree, I rank by the bursar or registrar figure and list the other.

## Ranking, highest to lowest

| # | School | Tuition | Mandatory fees | **Total** | Headline includes fees? | Source URL(s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **USC** (private, same rate for all) | $75,384 | $1,952 | **$77,336** | No, separate lines | https://financialaid.usc.edu/undergraduate-financial-aid/cost-of-attendance/ ; https://arr.usc.edu/tuition-and-fees/ |
